# Campus Library Reservation System (CLRS)  
## Assignment 2 — Architecture and Quality Plan

## 1. Context and scope

The Campus Library Reservation System (CLRS) replaces the existing study-room reservation tool across three university libraries. Students and staff can search for rooms and equipment, create or modify reservations, cancel reservations, and receive reminders. Library staff can manage rooms, opening hours, recurring block bookings, and utilisation reports. A kiosk outside each room displays its current and next reservation.

CLRS integrates with three important external systems:

- The university identity provider through SAML;
- Facilities calendars through iCal feeds;
- A legacy, read-only PostgreSQL room-inventory database.

The design must support the functional requirements FR-1 to FR-6 and the quality requirements QR-1 to QR-6. In particular, the system must provide 99.5% monthly availability during opening hours, return availability searches with a p95 latency below 400 ms for 2,000 concurrent users, authenticate users through SAML, audit staff actions without placing personally identifiable information in logs, support configuration-only onboarding of new campuses, allow reservation rules to be tested without a database or network, and be deployable and rolled back by a two-person team.
